page: Microsoft Azure M624ds_12_v3 is an x86_64 architecture server belonging to the MDSHighMemoryv3 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 624 dedicated vCPUs powered by Intel processors and is equipped with 11,400.0 GB of system memory, yielding approximately 18.27 GB of RAM per core. This high memory-to-vCPU ratio positions the instance within the ultra-high-memory tier of cloud resources.

For storage, the instance includes a 410 GB local SSD and is Premium Storage capable, allowing for high-throughput external storage attachments. There are zero GPUs integrated into this configuration, meaning all workloads rely entirely on the host CPU and memory architecture. No complimentary public IPv4 addresses are included with this server.

Given the massive scale of 624 vCPUs and over 11 TB of RAM, this server represents a highly specialized hardware class designed for extreme resource density. The qualitative cost profile reflects its position as an enterprise-grade, heavy-duty platform where consolidation of massive in-memory databases or large-scale enterprise resource planning systems justifies the infrastructure investment. Tradeoffs include the lack of hardware-accelerated graphics processing and a relatively small local SSD capacity of 410 GB relative to the massive memory size, requiring reliance on external Premium Storage for large persistent datasets. Appropriate workloads include massive in-memory databases, large-scale SAP HANA deployments, heavy data warehousing, and complex enterprise transactional workloads.
